questions.explanation: Multiplying $(\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{3})$ by $(\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3})$ gives $5 - 3 = 2$, a rational number, so $\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3}$ is the rationalising factor.

questions.body: If $p(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2x - 6$, find the remainder when $p(x)$ is divided by $(x - 3)$ using the Remainder Theorem.
questions.explanation: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder equals $p(3) = 27 - 27 + 6 - 6 = 0$. (This also shows $(x-3)$ is a factor of $p(x)$.)

questions.body: Using a suitable algebraic identity, factorise $x^3 + 8y^3 + 27z^3 - 18xyz$ completely, showing all steps.

answerKey.sampleAnswer: Using the identity $a^3 + b^3 + c^3 - 3abc = (a+b+c)(a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca)$ with $a = x$, $b = 2y$, $c = 3z$ (so $3abc = 3 \cdot x \cdot 2y \cdot 3z = 18xyz$), the expression becomes $(x + 2y + 3z)(x^2 + 4y^2 + 9z^2 - 2xy - 6yz - 3zx)$.
answerKey.rubric: 2 marks for correctly identifying the identity and the substitution $a=x, b=2y, c=3z$; 2 marks for verifying $3abc = 18xyz$; 2 marks for the correct final factorised form.
